title: Security review: pen test results & patching cadence - Crescent Bank
summary: Redwood and Crescent Bank reviewed the recent pen test findings, discussed risk categorization and remediation timeline, aligned on vuln mgmt process and patch cadence, and validated controls around RBAC/SSO, audit logs and KMS encryption. Next steps include sharing remediation tracker, customer to provide patching SOP and schedule a follow-up verification scan.
action_items: Jordan Lee - Share pen-test findings slide + remediation tracker (pen-test-results-2026-03-15.pdf) - due 2026-04-02
Nina Gomez - Provide current patching cadence and vulnerability management SOP - due 2026-04-07
Priya Patel - Run quick vuln scan against Redwood test pool and share results - due 2026-04-09
next_steps: Jordan to send remediation tracker and SOC2 docs link by 2026-04-02
Customer to share patching SLA/SOP and recent vulnerability backlog export by 2026-04-07
Schedule follow-up meeting w/ proof-of-patch verification week of 2026-04-13
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 09:30 PDT | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Allen (CISO, Crescent Bank), Nina Gomez (Security Engineer), Amit Shah (DevOps Manager), Lena O'Connor (VP Product)

Summary section (auto): Quick recap of pen test results and remediation priorities; discuss patch cadence and SDLC integration; confirm encryption/KMS and logging details.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, um, I know we circulated the pen-test report last week — I sent the deck and the tracker, hopefully folks had a chance to skim it.
[00:12] Marcus: Yeah thanks Jordan, we did, uh Nina and I went through high severity items. There's a couple things I want to make sure we get aligned on — particularly around patching windows and evidence for SOC 2.
[00:22] Priya: Cool; so today's agenda is, pen-test findings, remediation status/questions, vulnerability mgmt process, patch cadence, and then controls — RBAC/SSO, audit logs, KMS/encryption and data residency checks. We'll also capture next steps.
[00:35] Nina: One thing up front, some of the findings reference older AMIs in prod — we patched majority but there's still a few hosts in a private pool that Amit is investigating.
[00:45] Amit: Yeah sorry, that's on me; we have a staggered patching schedule to avoid cluster restart storm, so a few nodes lag. I can share the runbook after.
[00:53] Jordan: Great, please do. On the report, we marked those as "elevated" because exploitability was moderate but exposure to customer data is limited because of network segmentation. That said, we should confirm the timeframe for full remediation.
[01:06] Marcus: Target is two weeks for high but we need proof for our auditors, like a CVE patch log or ticket links.
[01:14] Priya: Understood — Redwood can provide evidence of the runtime image versions served to your environment and timestamps; we also keep audit logs for config changes per our retention policy. I'll outline what's available and formats.
[01:26] Lena: Quick Q: Is the audit logging at token level? We need to prove data handling for PCI scope conversation.
[01:33] Jordan: Good question — we capture API-level audit trails, request IDs, model/version, and token counts in logs; payloads are excluded from long-term logs by default but available in short-lived traces for debugging under strict access controls.
[01:47] Marcus: Can you confirm encryption keys — are they customer-managed KMS keys or Redwood-managed? For compliance, we prefer CMKs.
[01:56] Priya: For Private deployments yes CMK via customer KMS/HSM integration is supported. For Dedicated we offer BYOK for keys at rest. Hosted default is Redwood-managed but we can support a higher plan with customer keys.
[02:11] Nina: That's fine; Crescent is looking at a private control plane, so we'll need a KMS integration checklist.
[02:18] Jordan: We'll attach the KMS integration checklist to the tracker.

[02:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) so about the pen test, um, can you walk through the high-severity items again?
[02:38] Priya: Sure — there were three that we flagged high: 1) outdated library with known RCE path in the model serving side, 2) weak TLS config on a legacy internal endpoint that could let an attacker man-in-the-middle within same VPC, and 3) SAML assertion replay risk under a misconfiguration scenario. The exploitability varied; the RCE required local access but we treat it as high due to potential chain.
[02:58] Amit: For the library, we've already built a patch and validated in staging; rollout to prod will follow canary and we'll do smoke tests. The TLS endpoint was internal and we've tightened ciphers and rotated certs this morning.
[03:13] Nina: Good, can you link the commits/ticket? Auditors will want references.
[03:17] Amit: Yep will include GH ticket and PR.
[03:19] Jordan: I'll collect those and put into the remediation tracker as evidence.

[03:40] Marcus: On vuln mgmt process — what's your SLA for critical CVEs? How do you classify?
[03:46] Priya: We typically use CVSS and exploitability, then map to SLA tiers: Critical — patch within 7 days, High — 14 days, Medium — 30 days, but we are flexible and can codify customer-specific SLAs. For Dedicated/private customers, we can agree to stricter windows.
[04:02] Marcus: Right now Crescent's internal policy is 7 days for critical; we need Redwood to commit or at least provide timely mitigation steps.
[04:10] Jordan: We'll add remediation commit dates and mitigation workarounds to the tracker; Redwood also has an option for auto-rolled mitigations where feasible.

[04:26] Lena: Secure SDLC question: how does Redwood integrate dependency scanning and SCA for the serving code and model pipelines?
[04:33] Priya: We run dependency scans during CI — SCA tools, static analysis, and container image scanning. For model artifacts we have a vetting process and automated tests; higher-risk models go through an additional manual review.
[04:46] Marcus: Do you have SBOMs or provenance for runtime images?
[04:50] Priya: Yes, we can generate SBOMs for images and include them in release artifacts. We'll share the SBOM template.

[05:02] Jordan: (brief) we've attached a sample SBOM and the pen-test doc link in the meeting invite — file name pen-test-results-2026-03-15.pdf.

[05:12] Speaker 2 (customer): There's a note about RBAC — can you walk through user roles, and SSO provisioning?
[05:19] Priya: Sure; Redwood supports SAML/SCIM provisioning, role-based access with least-privilege roles, and audit logging for admin changes. For enterprise we can integrate your IdP and sync groups to roles.
[05:32] Nina: Do you support just-in-time access or step-up authentication?
[05:36] Priya: Not natively for JIT; we rely on IdP policies to enforce MFA and step-up. We can add session-expiry controls and short-lived admin tokens.

[05:49] Marcus: On the audit logs retention and export — what's the default retention and can we configure retention windows for our regulators?
[05:57] Jordan: Default is 90 days for detailed traces and 12 months for summary audit records; for enterprise customers we can extend retention and provide exports in raw or SIEM-ready formats (e.g., JSON/CEF).
[06:11] Nina: We need 2 years for certain controls. Is that doable?
[06:15] Jordan: Yes, that's on the enterprise add-on; we'll note requirements and pricing in the follow-up.

[06:25] Amit: Back to patch cadence — our challenge is rolling upgrades without impacting throughput. Your canary strategy, does it support connection draining and KV cache warmup?
[06:36] Priya: Yes, runtime supports phased rollouts with warmup hooks and KV cache migration strategies to avoid cold-start latency spikes. We'll share the canary runbook.
[06:45] Amit: Perfect. Also, what about emergency rollbacks if a patch causes performance regressions?
[06:50] Priya: We keep model version pinning and can rollback traffic quickly; we also have circuit-breaker fallbacks to a preserved baseline model variant.

[07:02] Marcus: Regarding data residency — Crescent needs EU-only processing for a subset of regulated customers. How does Redwood handle region pinning and audit?
[07:11] Jordan: Requests can be routed to specific regions and we provide region-scoped logs and datasets. For Private deployments you can deploy in your VPC in-region. We'll document the config options.

[07:25] Lena: One more — for SOC 2 evidence, what artifacts can Redwood provide?
[07:30] Jordan: SOC 2 report, encryption key logs (if BYOK enabled), audit log exports, change control tickets, SBOMs, and pen-test reports. We'll provide a consolidated evidence pack.

[07:44] Nina: On the pen-test remediation tracker, can we see assigned owners and proof links inline?
[07:49] Jordan: Yes, the tracker will have owner, status, evidence link (ticket/commit), and due date.

[08:00] Priya: Quick clarify — the SAML replay note: mitigation is to enforce token expiry and audience checks; we recommended rotating SAML certs and tightening assertion validity.
[08:12] Marcus: We'll coordinate with our IdP team.

[08:20] Jordan: Okay we're about halfway through the items — any blockers so far?
[08:24] Nina: Only that we need exact artifact formats for auditors — CSV for log exports, PDF for SOC report, links for commits.
[08:31] Jordan: Noted.

[08:40] Speaker 3: (background chatter)

[09:05] Priya: Also wanted to mention remediation sequencing — we advise triage of high items with temporary compensating controls first when immediate patching would cause outages. We'll document mitigations.
[09:18] Amit: That helps. For some infra-level changes we need change window approvals; mitigation could be network ACL rules to limit exposure.

[09:30] Marcus: Can Redwood provide a short slide for our board summarizing impact and timeline?
[09:36] Jordan: Yes, we can produce a 1-pager risk summary and timeline. We'll include the high/medium/low counts and planned dates.

[09:45] Priya: Another note on evidence — for CVE remediations we can provide vulnerability scanner reports (e.g., Nessus/Qualys) if you run a scan against our test pool; Redwood can also run an internal scan and share results under NDA.
[10:02] Nina: Let's do both — Crescent will run its scanner and Redwood to run internal.

[10:12] Jordan: Great — we'll coordinate scan windows in the tracker.

[10:20] Lena: About patch verification — will you mark items as "resolved" only after successful scan and ticket closure?
[10:26] Jordan: Yes, status will change to resolved after evidence is attached and both sides agree.

[10:35] Marcus: Ok, timeline recap — for the 4 high items you've committed to code patch + canary within 7 days?
[10:42] Priya: That's our plan; Amit confirmed staging validation is done for two of them.

[10:49] Amit: Two are already in canary, one is in staging and the TLS one we rotated certs already — so we should be mostly there.

[11:00] Jordan: Anything else on secure SDLC?
[11:04] Nina: One ask: include SCA scan outputs in release notes so we can spot regressions.
[11:09] Priya: We'll add SCA diff summary to release artifacts.

[11:16] Marcus: All right last bit — can Redwood commit to supporting our auditor with direct questions?
[11:22] Jordan: Yes, Redwood's security team can be made available for auditor calls under NDA; we'll coordinate availability.

[11:30] (closing) Jordan: To recap — Jordan to send remediation tracker + SOC docs by 2026-04-02; Nina to share patching SOP by 2026-04-07; Priya to run internal vuln scan and share results by 2026-04-09; follow-up meeting week of 2026-04-13. Any other items?
[11:45] Marcus: That's it from Crescent. Thanks team.
[11:49] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[11:51] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invite for verification scan.

End of transcript.
